hz9_power.topic: The power ledger: Hezbollah vs Israel, Lebanon vs Israel

claims.text: Nasrallah said in a speech on 18 Oct 2021, after the Tayouneh clashes, that Hezbollah had 100,000 trained fighters; AP: most estimates 25,000–50,000 including ~10,000 Radwan; experts called it exaggeration; Sarit Zehavi said greatly exaggerated.
Iran International: figure hard to verify; Lebanese armed forces estimated at about 85,000.
CSIS (2018): ~15,000 rockets before 2006, nearly 4,000 fired in 2006; arsenal estimated at 130,000 in 2018, mostly unguided.

USIP (Sep 2024): estimates up to 200,000 (some experts); Alma 75,000; mostly unguided; Hezbollah launched more than 8,800 rockets, missiles and drones at Israel in first year; Israel more than 8,000 strikes.
NYT (1 Oct 2024): pre-war stockpile estimated 120,000–200,000; senior Israeli and US officials said about half destroyed; tens of thousands remain.
JPost (10 Nov 2024) citing IDF: 80% of rockets up to 40 km destroyed; ~5,000 medium-range down to under 1,000; short-range 44,000+ to ~10,000; precision missiles from hundreds to under 100.
Alma (Nov 2024): pre-war ~75,000 rockets and missiles and ~2,500 drones; IDF destroyed at least 70–80%; 2,500–3,000 operatives killed.

ToI 12 Mar 2026: pre-war ~150,000; IDF said 70–80% of rocket capability destroyed in 2024 and later; Alma estimated ~25,000 before renewed fighting; several hundred medium/long-range missiles believed left.
IDF (March 2026): 85–90% of pre-2023 arsenal destroyed; ~30,000 remained in 2025; now 10,000–23,000; ~1,000 long-range precision rockets.

5 Apr 2026: Northern Command chief Rafi Milo acknowledged a 'gap' between how Northern Arrows was concluded and Hezbollah still standing; Channel 12: tens of thousands of rockets and hundreds of launchers; ~200 launches a day for about five more months; IDF says ~1,000 operatives killed since 2 Mar.
Nathan Sales (State Dept counterterrorism coordinator), Nov 2018: Iran gives Hezbollah some $700 million a year; Iran's proxy support near $1bn a year.
Funding estimates: $100–200m a year (earlier US estimates); $700m–$1bn (Wilson Center); Nasrallah acknowledged in Feb 2012 Iranian support since 1982 without a figure.
SIPRI: Israel 2025 military expenditure $48.3bn, down 4.9% real, 7.8% of GDP, 11th in world.
World Bank RDNA (8 Oct 2023–20 Dec 2024): $11bn needs; $14bn cost = $6.8bn damage + $7.2bn losses; housing damage $4.6bn; real GDP -7.1% in 2024; cumulative fall since 2019 near 40%.
RDNA summary: nominal GDP fell from about $55bn in 2018 to just over $20bn in 2023; 2024 fiscal surplus.

FDD (Kilcullen 2022): State Dept says more than $2.5bn in US security assistance to Lebanon since 2006 (21 May 2021 fact sheet); average ~$200m/yr; 2021 packages $105m + $15m + $67m; FY2022 request $160m; junior soldiers' pay fell to ~$100/month, one-eighth of pre-crisis.
